meta: Why do free AI app plans always have limits? Because every question costs real money. A normal app adds 1,000 users at almost no extra cost · an AI app pays for every token of every answer.

muc.title: A thousand more users
muc.text: For a normal app, a thousand more users costs almost nothing extra. AI apps are different: every question costs money.

muc.title: Every token costs money
muc.text: Because for every answer, the server has to run a giant model, working out each token. The longer the question and the more documents attached, the more it costs.

muc.title: The bill goes to the product maker
muc.text: Product makers pay the model company per million tokens. A large model can cost dozens of times, sometimes a hundred times, more than a small one.

muc.title: Why free plans have limits
muc.text: That's why free plans often limit messages per day, or only allow small models. Monthly plans are priced for the average user.

muc.title: Some people ask a thousand questions
muc.text: Some people ask a few questions a day, others run thousands. Heavy users can make a product lose money, so many "unlimited" plans still come with fair-use rules.

muc.title: A product maker's trick
muc.text: A product maker's trick: give easy tasks to a small model, and only call a large model for hard ones. For questions that come up a lot, save the answer so you don't have to work it out again.

muc.title: Check the pricing page
muc.text: Open the pricing page of an AI app you use. Where is the free plan limited? Now you know why it's limited exactly there.

muc.title: Part 6: When AI products stumble
muc.text: Cheap, fast and well designed, and it can still stumble badly. Part 6 tells three real stories.
